calibration: winner_in_my_two: YES — the named danger, again
column8: ERROR (one sentence): forty minutes after the master taught the Kempton lesson (class is the DNA of a Group race, the best horse is the one with the highest class achievement at level weights) I let a GROUND story — 'the only proven soft-ground Group winner' — outrank the only Group 1 winner in the field, and wrote at 14:31 that 'by that wording Almeraq is the class horse' while leaving Marvelman as the pick because he was already banked; the class horse won by four lengths and the ground horse finished last
column9: CALIBRATION: (1) THE LESSON WAS ON THE PAGE BEFORE THE RACE AND NOT APPLIED: a banked pick cannot be changed (the record is the record), but the sheet's own class line said Almeraq and the ground line said Marvelman, and the day had already ruled which outranks which — the order of facts is CLASS first, then the race's DNA, then ground/course/trip; a G2-winner-on-soft is a lower class line than a G1-winner-on-firm. (2) THE BOOKIES AGAIN: three at 3/1-7/2 with the G1 winner the 3/1 one — the market was not tricking anyone here; the class horse was the favourite by a shade and I read 'the market cannot separate them' as a licence to pick the story. (3) Sittings today, final: 1 from 5 (Rocket Boy 2nd, Archers Bay 3rd, Gethin 2nd, AEGEAN PRINCE WON, Marvelman last) plus the duty's Proposal 2nd — 1 from 6; the named danger or second danger WON five of the six; every one of those five had the best form line at the highest class in its race. The read finds the winner; the verdict must take the best class line, not the best story.
